earlier_scan.source_named: Sign language (Keresan Pueblo Indian Sign Language); no spoken word-stress description exists; only Kelley 2001 sociolinguistic book and Nyst 2014 note.

sources.citation: Kelley, Walter P. & Tony L. McGregor. 2003. Keresan Pueblo Indian Sign Language. In J. Reyhner, O. Trujillo, R. L. Carrasco & L. Lockard (eds.), Nurturing Native Languages, 141-148. Flagstaff, AZ: Northern Arizona University.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic/lexical description of a village sign language (origin, users, sample signs). No prosody/stress discussion; the words 'stress', 'accent', 'prosody' do not occur. Word stress in the spoken-language sense is not applicable to a signed language.

sources.citation: Kelley, Walter P. 2001. Pueblo Individuals Who are D/deaf: Acceptance in the Home Community, the Dominant Society, and the Deaf Community. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Austin.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only book-length work on KPISL and its users; would confirm there is no structural/prosodic description. Low value for a word-stress catalog since the language is signed.
